summary: Peter van der Veer is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Groningen and Utrecht University, later serving as professor at Utrecht, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, University of Amsterdam, and director at the Max Planck Institute (~2009–2021).

Peter von Bohlen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Halle, Bonn, and Berlin under Georg Freytag, August Wilhelm von Schlegel, and Franz Bopp. He served as professor of oriental literature at the University of Königsberg from 1825.

Peter von Bradke was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Dorpat/Tartu, Tübingen, Jena, Leipzig, and Giessen, under scholars including Leo Meyer and Rudolf von Roth. He served as associate professor at the University of Giessen (1886–1896).

Peter von Köppen was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the National University of Kharkiv (~1808–1814) and the University of Tübingen (~1822–1823), and served at the Ministry of State Property (~1837–1860).

Petra Kieffer-Pülz is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Heinz Bechert (~1985–1991). She held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1989–2001) and the Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur Mainz (~2002).

Petra Maurer is a Tibetologist who studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. Her posts include positions at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013, 2026) and the University of Munich (attested 2018).

Phakchok Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who earned a Khenpo title at Dzongsar Institute (~1995–2004) under numerous traditional teachers. He became Vajra Master at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling Monastery around 2004.

Pham Thi Tuyet Tam is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, studying under supervisors Phra Maha Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull (attested 2017).

Phanit Jetjiravat is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under academic advisors Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

Philip A. Kuhn was a sinologist and historian. He studied at Harvard, SOAS, and Georgetown, and later held posts as associate professor of history at the University of Chicago (1963–1978) and professor and center director at Harvard University (1978; 1980–1986).

Philip A. Mellor is a religious studies scholar who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Manchester in 1989. He has served as Professor of Religion and Social Theory at the University of Leeds (attested 2010).

Philip B. Yampolsky was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned his degrees from Columbia University and studied under Yoshitaka Iriya, later serving as an adjunct associate professor, librarian, and lecturer at Columbia (1968–1996).

Philip Clart is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied under Daniel L. Overmyer (~1991–1996) and became Professor of Chinese Culture and History at the University of Leipzig around 2008.
Philip Deslippe is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He has served as a graduate student and teaching associate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2020–2026).

Philip Kapleau was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Soen Nakagawa, Daiun Sogaku Harada, and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani between 1950 and 1967. He founded the Rochester Zen Center and Chapin Mill Retreat Center.

Philip L. Quinn was a philosopher who studied at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh. He served on the faculty at Brown University (~1971–1985) and as John A. O'Brien Professor of Philosophy at the University of Notre Dame from 1985.

Philip Lutgendorf is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Chicago (~1967–1987) and served on the faculty at the University of Iowa from 1985, as well as president of AIIS (2010–2018).

Philip Novak is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Notre Dame (~1968–1972) and Syracuse University (~1976–1981), and began teaching at Dominican University of California around 1980.

Philip Whalen was a Buddhist studies practitioner and poet who earned a BA from Reed College and studied under Richard Baker. He served as head monk at Dharma Sangha (1984) and abbot at Hartford Street Zen Center (1991).

Philipp André Maas is an Indologist and philosopher. He completed his PhD at the University of Bonn under Claus Vogel and Albrecht Wezler, later holding research posts at the University of Vienna, Austrian Academy of Sciences, and University of Leipzig.
